title: Auth Control Plane credential issue/rotate receipt (v1 wire format)
description:
The response of POST /v1/credentials/issue and POST /v1/credentials/{id}/rotate, and the ONLY credential representation that may carry a secret value, once (TRD section 12). It is a separate schema rather than an entry with a conditionally present field, so the asymmetry is visible in the file layout and a secret can never be added to a list or an entry by widening one conditional.

kind=rotate requires credential.rotation_parent_id (lineage is what makes 'rotation preserves or narrows privilege' auditable); kind=issue forbids it. The secret begins with the credential's display_prefix (a client rule: a schema cannot compare two members); display_prefix is the only fragment of the secret that appears anywhere else. This schema describes registry METADATA: owner, class, domain authority, audiences, scopes, fingerprint and display prefix, status, timestamps and rotation lineage. A secret is unrepresentable here, not merely optional: the object is closed and has no secret, hash or token member. The members are the columns of credential_registry (migration 0003 plus 0007) minus the secret-bearing secret_hash and hash_algorithm, plus the derived status; TestCredentialEntryMatchesTheRegistryColumnsInBothDirections derives both sets from the migrations and fails on any difference. Scope: ACR and External Push credentials appear only as metadata projections (ACP-ADR-08/09).

id.description: Server-minted credential id (the registry row's id). New prefix introduced by this contract.

credential_class.description: The platform's closed credential-class vocabulary, the same enum principal.v1 carries; a test fails if the two drift.

display_prefix.description: The ONLY fragment of a secret that may appear anywhere but the one-time receipt: at most 16 characters, pinned by the schema rather than left to a producer. Not secret, not sufficient to authenticate.

fingerprint.description: Non-secret fingerprint of the credential's public identifier: 16 lowercase hex characters. Required on a new credential (receipts); absent only on rows that predate migration 0007.

domain_owner.description: Which validator owns the credential. ACR and External Push keep their domain validators (ACP-ADR-08/09): this is a metadata projection, never a second validator or writer.

external_reference.description: The domain system's own id for a projected credential. Opaque; present exactly when domain_owner is not platform.

scopes.description: Scopes in principal.v1's shape (colon-separated); a set.

rotation_parent_id.description: The credential this one rotated from (TRD section 12). Required on a rotate receipt, absent on an issue receipt.

status.description: DERIVED, not stored: revoked_at set -> revoked; else expires_at <= now -> expired; else active. The schema pins status to the timestamps' shape; the comparison with the clock is a client rule.

credential.description: The issued credential's registry metadata at issue time: active, with its fingerprint, no usage or revocation members.

secret.description: The one-time secret value: 32..256 URL-safe characters. Its alphabet is a superset of display_prefix's, so every prefix the entry allows can begin a valid secret (a closure test builds a receipt from every allowed prefix shape). Never repeated by any other schema, log or audit row.
